name: Guadalajara Cathedral
scope: The standing Cathedral of the Assumption of Mary in Guadalajara, including its symmetrical western towers, principal basilican mass and roof, and attached eastern volumes. The separately named Sagrario Metropolitano is excluded.
era: The standing cathedral in the 2008 and 2022 exterior photographs, with the nineteenth-century replacement spires.

originalReview.notes: Daylight view from behind the cathedral. Shows warm stone, the pale yellow and cream tapered spire faces, pinnacle edges and eastern roof context. The identifiable arcade of the neighboring Sagrario is kept outside the model.

West plaza evening view establishes the segmented central pediment, clock crown, portal spacing, open bell stages and alternating faces of the two pointed spires. Evening illumination is not used to infer daylight colors.
